Valentine's Day has 3 distinct genuine PLPs with non-identical, non-subset product sets (gifts-shop-for-valentines-day 39, valentines-day-gifts-for-her 33, valentines-day-gifts-for-him 29) - all three kept as siblings. Excluded as non-genuine-category or marketing: gifts-stocking-stuffers (site's own title labels it 'Gift Guide'); holiday-art-print-offers (a '15% off, code ART15' discount promo page); 12-days-for-presents-with-presence and 12-days-of-gifting-30-off-furniture-lighting-rugs (Christmas sale campaign pages, 1 and 0 products); new-holiday (1-product 'new arrivals' teaser, its sole item already covered under Menorahs); spring-makeover-event and a-mid-winter-wink-sale-styles (sale events, hit the 250-item cap / 0 products); new-trending-summer-styles, summer-styles, select-summer-styles (seasonal-styled merchandising, not a site-defined Summer holiday category - select-summer-styles' own title is a 'Buy One Get One 30% Off' promo); and the four Valentine's Day price-tier pages (-for-50ish/100ish/200ish/over-the-top-valentines-day-gifts), excluded per the shared core's 'price filter pages are not categories' rule. Also excluded ~60 generic gifts-by-recipient/gifts-by-price collections (Mom/Dad/Her/Him/Wedding/Housewarming/Baby/Host/Jonathan's Go-To) as evergreen recipient/price gift filters with no calendar-seasonal tie. Qty obtained via each collection's own /products.json?limit=250 Shopify endpoint, counting unique product handles - a full enumeration since every collection returned under the 250 cap; the rendered page HTML is client-side PLP with no visible 'N products' count, so the structured-data/full-enumeration tier of the qty method was used.
